label: Degree of a perfection and capacity…: Deg y r: the degree in which y has the perfection r; cap z…
term: degree of a perfection and capacity for it (deg y r, cap z r)
definition: deg y r: the degree in which y has the perfection r; cap z r: the measure of r that z can take. Both lie in one preorder of degrees per batch (a parameter D with a Mathlib Preorder). This is a measure reading of 'to the measure of z's capacity' in DEF-PERFECTION-LIMITED-BY. Example: the heat of the fire exceeds what the wood can take; the wood's heat is within it. Nothing makes degrees of different respects comparable, and nothing here says every two degrees are comparable: the open premise STMT-UNLIMITED-HAVING-EXCEEDS-CAPACITY carries the comparability it needs. Degrees are not quantities in a physical sense.
note: Stipulative analyst notion, attribution deferred. Constrained only by STMT-LIMITED-HAVING-IS-WITHIN-CAPACITY, STMT-UNLIMITED-HAVING-EXCEEDS-CAPACITY and STMT-GREATER-DEGREE-IS-MORE. A source would be a passage that measures perfections by degree (ST I q.2 a.3 quarta via 'magis et minus'; q.3 a.5 ad 2 'tantum habet de esse'); no claim is made here.
